subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit persistent hook-agent sessions, and what hook auth, agent, session-key, and prefix boundaries must gate https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 before it can land?
rationale: The remaining fix changes how external hook requests can re-enter durable agent context, so the permanent API and security boundary need maintainer intent rather than a new automatic fix lane.

options.title: Land Explicit Persistent Mode
options.body: Accept `sessionMode: "persistent"` as an opt-in while keeping omitted mode isolated and requiring existing hook auth, allowed-agent, prefix, docs, and regression proof.

options.title: Keep Hooks Isolated
options.body: Reject persistent hook-agent sessions for now and update docs/API wording so webhook callers do not expect multi-turn continuity.

options.title: Choose Another API Shape
options.body: Pause the current PR and specify a narrower compatibility-safe surface such as a trusted binding or session-target policy.

recommendation.title: Land Explicit Persistent Mode
recommendation.body: Accept `sessionMode: "persistent"` as an opt-in while keeping omitted mode isolated and requiring existing hook auth, allowed-agent, prefix, docs, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already framed the issue-level `sessionMode` direction and has the strongest review-history signal for the product/security boundary choice.
